page: Microsoft Azure E128ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor architecture, the instance supplies 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1024.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. It includes 7560 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage capabilities, while omitting discrete GPU acceleration.

The combination of dedicated compute cores, large memory density, and 7.5 TB of low-latency NVMe scratch space addresses resource-intensive applications that require high I/O throughput alongside substantial memory footprints. Cost efficiency is driven by the co-location of high-capacity local temporary storage with enterprise-grade compute and memory resources, reducing dependencies on external storage tiers for intermediate data buffering.

This hardware configuration is suited for enterprise relational database engines, massive in-memory analytics workloads, distributed caching tiers, and large-scale ETL data pipelines requiring significant RAM and high-speed temporary storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E128ds_v6 is a high-capacity, memory-optimized virtual machine designed for demanding enterprise enterprise workloads. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V with x86_64 Intel processing hardware, this instance delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key architectural element is the inclusion of 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside Premium Storage capabilities, offering fast temporary I/O without requiring auxiliary storage hardware. The instance lacks discrete GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its capabilities entirely toward compute, memory, and high-speed local data handling. From an operational efficiency perspective, the integration of high-density memory and 7.5 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage optimizes large transactional processing costs. The platform is well matched for in-memory databases, large-scale relational database engines, real-time analytics platforms, and intensive extract, transform, load operations.
